title.value: Nanoscale Ru unlocking nanoneedles assembled into hierarchical CoO microspheres for efficient nitrate-to-ammonia electroconversion.

abstract.value: Because of the strong ability of cobalt oxide (CoO) to render active hydrogen (*H) for selective hydrogenation of NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup>, it is well established as a promising catalyst for the electrocatalytic reduction of NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup> to ammonia (eRNO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup>-to-NH<sub>3</sub>) for green NH<sub>3</sub> synthesis along with NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup> pollutant treatment. Unfortunately, its practical application is severely limited by easy agglomeration, weak NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup> adsorption, and the side reaction of H* coupling, causing the blockage of active sites and low selectivity of NH<sub>3</sub>. For this, we purposefully designed a hetero hybrid electrocatalyst (denoted as CoO-Ru/CC), where nano-dimensional metallic Ru is anchored onto nanoneedles assembled into hierarchical CoO microspheres that are self-supported on carbon cloth (CC). Because of the vertical order open architecture, intrinsic oxygen vacancies, and local electric field in the self-standing CoO-Ru heterostructure, there are abundant active sites, efficient adsorption of NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup>, weakened N-O bonds, and a reduced reaction energy barrier, as well
